knowledge_point.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosine Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
The period of $y=\cos x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have

$$
\cos x=\cos (x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\cos x=\cos (x+2\cdot 1\cdot \pi )=\cos (x+2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\cos x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},$ then $\cos (x+2\pi )=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$

question.:question/worked-solution:

The period of $y=\cos x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have

$$
\cos x=\cos (x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-3$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\cos x=\cos (x+2\cdot (-3)\cdot \pi )=\cos (x-6\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\cos x=-\frac{7}{11},$ then $\cos (x-6\pi )=-\frac{7}{11}.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The period of $y=\cos x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have

$$
\cos x=\cos (x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\cos x=\cos (x+2\cdot 2\cdot \pi )=\cos (x+4\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\cos x=\frac{1}{10},$ then $\cos (x+4\pi )=\frac{1}{10}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cos (x+4\pi )+4 & =6(\frac{1}{10})+4 \\  & =\frac{3}{5}+4 \\  & =\frac{23}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
